title: test_api08_auth.zig's tenant_default recovery path DROP SCHEMA CASCADE races concurrent zig build test binaries, causing widespread process_definitions/users/api_tokens C42P01 failures
reporter: BACKEND-DEV (WF03-ISS-0130-20260807, Step 03 regression verification for ISS-0130/GH #423)
notes: Discovered while running the mandatory `zig build test --summary all` regression comparison for ISS-0130 (GH #423). Reproduced identically (byte-for-byte same 21 failing test names) on THREE separate runs: twice on the ISS-0130 feature branch and once on a clean `origin/main` worktree baseline with no ISS-0130-related changes at all -- proving this is 100% pre-existing on main and completely unrelated to the search_path/SET LOCAL fix. Deterministic, not flaky: same failure set across all 3 runs (918/1003 passing, 21 failing, every time).
root_cause: tests/unit/test_api08_auth.zig's ensureTenantDefaultSchema() helper (lines 62-96) calls provisionTenantSchema() for tenant_default, and on ANY MigrationFailed error (which can be caused by transient contention with another concurrently-running test binary in the same `zig build test` graph -- not just genuine corruption) falls back to an unconditional `DROP SCHEMA IF EXISTS tenant_default CASCADE` (line 78) followed by re-provisioning. `zig build test` runs many binaries concurrently by default (this is the aggregate 'all unit tests' step covering ~80+ compile+run steps), and several other files (including tests/integration/helpers.zig's TestHarness.init() and other tests/unit/*.zig files) also provision or depend on the SAME shared tenant_default schema existing. When test_api08_auth's recovery path fires mid-run, it destroys tenant_default -- and every table in it (process_definitions, users, api_tokens, user_roles, etc.) -- out from under any other binary that is concurrently relying on that schema already being provisioned, producing C42P01 'relation X does not exist' in whichever sibling binary happens to query it in that window. definition_retrieval_test.zig (tests/unit/, also DB-backed, also depends on tenant_default's process_definitions table) is the most visible collateral victim, but the underlying defect is entirely inside test_api08_auth.zig's destructive recovery path, not in definition_retrieval_test.zig itself (which was already hardened for a DIFFERENT concurrency issue in ISS-0141 / GH #445 -- unique fixture names -- and that fix remains correct; this is a new, different failure mode: the whole schema disappearing, not a fixture collision).
repro_steps: 1. zig build test --summary all (fresh or shared BPM_TEST_DB_URL, either works)
2. Observe Build Summary: 918/1003 tests passed, 21 failed

3. All 21 failures are in definition_retrieval_test.zig (TC-PD-07-*) and test_api08_auth.zig (TC-IDN-01-06, TC-IDN-04-04a/b, TC-IDN-04-05a/b), each showing C42P01 on process_definitions/users/api_tokens/user_roles inside the tenant_default schema
4. Reproduces identically on a clean origin/main worktree with zero other changes
candidate_resolution: Either (a) make ensureTenantDefaultSchema's recovery path serialize against other concurrent provisioners of tenant_default via the existing pg_advisory_lock keyed by tenant_id (already added for ISS-0131 in provisionTenantSchema, but this DROP SCHEMA happens OUTSIDE that lock's critical section, after provisionTenantSchema has already returned an error and released its own lock), or (b) stop treating a generic MigrationFailed as sufficient evidence of corruption warranting a destructive DROP -- distinguish 'this schema is genuinely broken' from 'a concurrent caller is mid-provisioning it and I raced them', e.g. by re-checking migrations_applied_at IS NOT NULL before concluding a DROP is warranted, or (c) move test_api08_auth.zig's DB-touching tests out of tests/unit/ (anti-patterns.md already documents DB-backed tests in tests/unit/ as a violation) and into tests/integration/ where they can use the shared TestHarness/advisory-lock machinery instead of a bespoke recovery path.
acceptance_criteria: AC-1: zig build test passes 100% deterministically across 5 consecutive runs with no process_definitions/users/api_tokens C42P01 failures

AC-2: The destructive DROP SCHEMA recovery path in test_api08_auth.zig either no longer exists, or is provably safe under concurrent zig build test execution (e.g. via an advisory lock held across the whole check-then-drop-then-reprovision sequence)
prevention: A recovery path that destroys shared state on error should hold whatever lock protects that shared state for its ENTIRE check-then-act sequence, not just for the initial provisioning attempt that failed.

DB-backed tests belong in tests/integration/, not tests/unit/, specifically so they get the shared TestHarness/advisory-lock protections that tests/unit/ files (each rolling their own ad-hoc setup) do not have.
prior_iss_search: Related but distinct: ISS-0141/GH #445 (definition_retrieval_test.zig fixture-name collisions, already RESOLVED and NOT reintroduced -- current failures are a different symptom, the whole schema disappearing, not a fixture unique-constraint collision) and GH #457/#477 (other tenant_default provisioning races, already CLOSED, different specific mechanisms). No prior ISS covers test_api08_auth.zig's own DROP SCHEMA recovery path racing concurrent binaries.
